title: Street Style Chole with Crispy Potatoes
description: Delhi-inspired street-style chole served with crispy spiced potatoes, mint yogurt, pickled onions, and fresh herbs. Rich, spicy, tangy, and perfect as a hearty bowl.
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the diced potatoes with oil, cornstarch, paprika, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt. Roast for 30–35 minutes, flipping halfway, until deeply golden and crispy.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion until deeply golden, about 10–12 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the blended tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook until the mixture thickens and the oil begins separating.
Stir in the chole masala, coriander powder, roasted cumin, Kashmiri chilli powder, turmeric, amchur, anardana (if using), and salt. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and vegetable stock. Simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes.
Mash a small portion of the chickpeas against the side of the pot to naturally thicken the gravy.
Finish with crushed Kasoori methi and adjust the seasoning with additional salt or lemon juice if needed.
For the pickled onions, toss the sliced red onion with lemon juice and sumac or chaat masala. Let sit for at least 10 minutes.
Blend the Greek yogurt, mint, cilantro, green chili, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt until smooth.
To serve, spoon the hot chole into a bowl. Top with the crispy potatoes, pickled onions, mint yogurt, chopped cilantro, and a fresh mint sprig.
notes: For authentic Delhi street-style flavor, simmer the chole for at least 30 minutes after adding the chickpeas.
Adding a small tea bag while simmering darkens the chole naturally; remove it before serving.
Roasting the potatoes instead of frying makes them crisp while using much less oil.
The bowl pairs well with toasted pita, kulcha, naan, or even basmati rice.
A final sprinkle of chaat masala and a squeeze of fresh lemon just before serving brightens all the flavors.
